summary: mountainash-rules is designed for extensibility across match strategies, aggregate operations, hit policies, and backends. The codebase follows consistent patterns that make it straightforward to add new capabilities while maintaining cross-backend correctness. Dependency direction is enforced one-way: engines/accumulator -> engines/filter -> core.
use_cases: Add a new match strategy to support a domain-specific comparison (e.g. geographic proximity, semantic similarity).
Extend the accumulator engine with additional aggregate operations beyond sum/min/max/product.
Add a new hit policy for a selection semantic not covered by collect/unique/first/priority/any/rule_order.
Contribute cross-backend test coverage for new or existing strategies.
Improve expression compilation for better performance on a specific backend.

concepts.name: Adding a new MatchStrategy
concepts.description: The end-to-end process for a new strategy follows a clear path (CLAUDE.md 'Adding a strategy'): add the enum value in core/constants.py, add validation logic in core/dimension.py, implement _compile_<strategy> in core/compiler.py, and add a corresponding test class in tests/core/test_compiler.py. EXACT_KEY and the REGEX/CONTEXT_REGEX split are recent examples of this pattern.

concepts.name: Adding an accumulator strategy
concepts.description: AccumulatorCompiler now supports EXACT, RANGE, GT/LT threshold, and SET_MEMBERSHIP/SET_EXCLUSION. To add support for another strategy, implement the corresponding cases in compile_compatible (the compatibility guard) and compile_coalesce (the value-merge logic).

concepts.name: Adding a new aggregate operation
concepts.description: AggregateOp now has four commutative, associative operations: sum, min, max, product. Adding a fifth means extending AggregateOp and the level-expansion aggregation logic in AccumulatorEngine. Note the documented limitation: aggregate-value overflow is backend-defined and unguarded (only the __prime_product identity is int64-guarded).

concepts.name: Adding a hit policy
concepts.description: HitPolicy is a StrEnum (collect/unique/first/priority/any/rule_order). New policies add an ordering_keys case and, if the policy asserts cardinality, a check_assertions/apply_cardinality case in core/hit_policy.py.

concepts.name: Backend-agnostic expression patterns
concepts.description: All compiler output uses the mountainash BaseExpressionAPI, ensuring expressions work across every supported backend. Use t_col, t_eq, t_ne and related helpers for sentinel-aware ternary comparisons, and ma.when/then/otherwise for conditional logic. Staying within these abstractions guarantees cross-backend compatibility -- and is enforced package-wide by tests/test_backend_purity.py.

concepts.name: Set-dimension wildcard pattern
concepts.description: New shared module: set dimensions represent 'wildcard' as an in-band '[sentinel]' list rather than null, normalized at ingestion (normalize_set_expr) and validated for reservation (validate_set_columns) and null elements (validate_set_no_null_elements) in both engines. Any new set-aware strategy should reuse these helpers rather than reinventing set-sentinel handling.

concepts.name: Test patterns
concepts.description: The test tree mirrors the src/ package layout (tests/core/, tests/filter/, tests/accumulator/, tests/benchmarks/). tests/filter/test_engine.py is the primary template for backend-parameterised evaluation tests; tests/accumulator/test_backends.py covers the accumulator engine. New strategies and features should follow these patterns to ensure coverage across all backends.
